title: Regional token surge sweep and GPU rotation plan - 2026
content:
Executive summary:
This planning sheet enumerates a set of realistic surge scenarios for the Hosted API, translates token/sec and QPS forecasts into GPU-slice requirements by region, and prescribes a short rotation + safety stock policy to keep 99th percentile latency SLOs during sudden spikes. This is an operational worksheet for infra on-call and capacity planning; not a finalized contract doc.

Key objectives:
- Define target headroom for P95 and P99 peak events (tokens/sec and QPS) by region.
- Map headroom to GPU-slice count and list warm-standby pools.
- Describe a GPU rotation and reclaim policy for underutilized pools to reduce wasted reserved capacity.
- Actionable runbook entries for surge (>2x baseline) and extreme spike (>5x baseline).

Assumptions and constants (current operating model):
- Average tokens per request: 120 tokens (chat + few-shot prompts).
- Average tokens/sec per request at streaming steady-state: ~30 tokens/sec during generation window.
- Baseline request pattern: 60% short completions (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64-256), 10% long (>256).
- Typical model mix: 60% Llama2-13B-q4, 30% mix of smaller quantized variants, 10% 70B class for high-quality flows.
- GPU slice: 1 slice = 1xA100-80GB-equivalent serving capacity for median workload (not for 70B).
- Warm-standby spin-up time (to usable): 90s average for a kept-warm VM + model preload; 18s for container hot-swap when model already loaded.

Regional baseline and forecast (current usage -> 2026Q3 peak estimates):
Columns: Region | Current baseline tokens/sec | P95 peak tokens/sec (1-in-30 day) | P99 peak tokens/sec (1-in-100 day) | Baseline GPU slices | Headroom target (P95) slices | Headroom target (P99) slices
US-WEST1 | 320k | 720k | 1.4M | 40 | 90 | 170
US-EAST1 | 420k | 920k | 1.9M | 52 | 115 | 230
EU-WEST1 | 190k | 420k | 820k | 24 | 54 | 106
AP-SOUTHEAST1 | 95k | 220k | 420k | 12 | 28 | 54
SOUTH-AM (preview) | 32k | 72k | 150k | 4 | 10 | 20

Notes on mapping tokens/sec -> GPU slices:
- Mapping uses conservative per-slice sustained throughput of ~8k tokens/sec for mixed workload (accounting for KV-cache misses and long-seq tail).
- For model mixes with 70B class, we account separately: the 70B steady traffic is capped and requires dedicated slices (not included in the general slice mapping above).

Safety stock and rotation policy recommendations:
- Safety stock = max(ceil(Headroom(P99) - baseline_slices), ceil(20% of baseline_slices)). This ensures a minimum buffer for small regions.
- Maintain a warm-standby pool equal to 25% of P95 headroom in region (kept with model preloads across top-3 serving models). Warm pool allows ~90s recovery.
- Cross-region borrow: allow borrowing up to 15% of idle slices from adjacent regions when cross-region latency impact is acceptable.
- Rotation cadence: evaluate underutilized slices weekly; if a slice has <10% average CPU/GPU utilization and <500 requests/day for 7 continuous days, mark for rotation/repurpose.

Degraded-mode routing (if P99 exceeds capacity despite safety stock):
- Step 1 (graceful degradation): Route low-priority traffic (internal/debugging, scheduled jobs) to burst pool or queue; enforce strict token caps per request to reduce tail latency.
- Step 2 (quality fallback): Automatically switch 70B-class flows to high-quality 13B quantized fallback when 70B capacity is saturated.
- Step 3 (regional fallback): Fall back to replicated regional model variant with reduced context length (truncate prompts) to preserve throughput.

Operational runbook snippets (for on-call):
- Surge alert thresholds: tokens/sec crossing 1.6x baseline sustained for 2 minutes -> P95 alert; crossing 3.5x baseline for 30s -> P99 alert.
- Immediate mitigations: increase per-region autoscaler floor by +20% (manual override), activate warm-standby preloads for top-3 models, throttle non-customer routes via rate-limiter.
- If after 4 minutes service at 95th latency still > target, trigger cross-region borrowing and notify product (expected customer-facing feature impact).

Cost vs reliability tradeoffs (short analysis):
- Keeping warm-standby at 25% P95 headroom increases committed monthly GPU cost by ~12% but reduces cold-start latency incidents by >90%.
- Cross-region borrowing saves committed capacity but increases egress and inter-region transfer latency; limit to non-latency-critical tenants.

Recommended short-term actions (next 30 days):
- (Owner: Ethan Chen) Implement automated weekly utilization report per-slice and flag rotation candidates.
- (Owner: Priya Singh) Provision warm-standby pools in AP-SOUTHEAST1 and SOUTH-AM for the next 60 days trial.
- (Owner: Maya Patel) Add P99 headroom delta metric to the infra dashboard and create a visual "surge heat" map by region.
- (Owner: SRE on-call) Draft a playbook for graceful degradation with traffic-class tags and test in staging with 2x synthetic spike.

Longer-term recommendations (Q3 2026 planning):
- Move to per-customer QoS tokens accounting and preemptible backfill pools to reduce hard reserved slices.
- Expand model compilation/quantization program to reduce per-slice tokens/sec to 10k sustained for median workload (target improvement).

Open questions / risks:
- How many customers are sensitive to cross-region reroute? Need product input to set per-tenant tolerance flags.
- Accurate per-slice throughput for mixed 70B + quantized mixes still uncertain; recommend targeted benchmarks on restricted workloads.
- Preemptible GPU economics vs reserved capacity tradeoffs for sustained regional peaks.

Attachment style appendix (worksheet tables to be converted into sheet columns):
- Column suggestions: region, baseline_tokens_per_sec, p95_tokens_per_sec, p99_tokens_per_sec, baseline_slices, p95_slices, p99_slices, warm_pool_target, cross_region_borrow_limit, last_rotation_date, notes
